# List of Figures, Tables, and Apps

A consolidated index of every numbered figure and table in the book, plus the interactive Shiny apps. Click any entry to jump to it in context.

## List of Shinylive Apps

* @fig-inverse-cdf-app — Shinylive App Illustrating the Inverse CDF Method.
* @fig-nr-divergence-app — Shinylive App Illustrating Newton–Raphson Divergence.
* @fig-gradient-methods-app — Shinylive App Comparing Gradient Descent and Newton-Raphson Optimization Algorithms.
* @fig-nelder-mead-app — Shinylive App Illustrating Nelder–Mead.
* @fig-sgd-app — Shinylive App for Stochastic Gradient Descent.
* @fig-mixture-app — Shinylive App Illustrating the EM Algorithm for a Normal Mixture.
* @fig-bayes-explorer-app — Shinylive App Illustrating Conjugate Bayesian Updating.
* @fig-missed-mode-nq-app — Shinylive App Illustrating a Quadrature Grid Missing the Posterior Mode.
* @fig-laplace-transform-app — Shinylive App Illustrating Adaptive Gauss–Hermite Quadrature.
* @fig-rejection-app — Shinylive App Illustrating Envelope Tightness in Rejection Sampling.
* @fig-gamma-rejection-app — Shinylive App Illustrating Rejection Sampling from a Gamma Density with a Cauchy Envelope.
* @fig-ars-app — Shinylive App Illustrating Adaptive Rejection Sampling.
* @fig-missed-mode-app — A Shinylive App Illustrating the Failure of Importance Sampling.
* @fig-t-is-app — Shinylive App for Importance Sampling of a Student-$t$ Interval.
* @fig-marlik-app — Shinylive App for Sorted Importance Weights.
* @fig-hmc-app — Shinylive App Illustrating Hamiltonian Monte Carlo Tuning.

## List of Figures

### Introduction to Statistical Computation

* @fig-sampling-distributions — Two sampling distributions for the same target $\theta$: $\hat\theta^{(1)}$ is biased with large variance, $\hat\theta^{(2)}$ is unbiased with small variance.
* @fig-null-alternative-distributions — Null ($H_0$) and alternative ($H_1$) distributions of a test statistic $T$, with the type I error, power, and $p$-value shown as tail areas.
* @fig-intro-prior-likelihood-posterior — A vague prior, the likelihood, and the resulting posterior for a normal mean: the posterior sits close to the likelihood, slightly narrower and pulled a little toward the prior mean.
* @fig-uniform-sum-hist — Simulated distribution of $X_1 + X_2$ for independent $\text{Unif}(0,1)$ variables, from 10,000 draws: a Monte Carlo approximation to the (triangular) true density.
* @fig-gamma-maximizer — A Gamma(3,1) density: its maximizer $x_0$ is obvious by eye, unlike a multi-parameter log-likelihood.
* @fig-quadrature-rectangles — Numerical quadrature by rectangle rule: approximating the area under a Gamma(3,1) density with 12 midpoint rectangles.

### Introduction to R and Quarto

* @fig-course-score-hist — Distribution of course scores across the class, with the class average marked in red.
* @fig-course-score-by-program — Course score by academic program, with individual scores jittered over the boxplots.
* @fig-final-vs-quiz-by-program — Final exam score versus mean quiz score, by program, with a fitted regression line per program revealing the built-in intercept offset.

### Computer Arithmetic

* @fig-toy-lines — Positive numbers at zoom $e=0$ (top, gap $0.1$) and $e=+1$ (bottom, gap $1$).
* @fig-log1mexp — The three implementations of log(1 - exp(-u)) against u on a log scale.

### Random Numbers and Monte Carlo Methods

* @fig-lcg-vs-runif — A hand-rolled linear congruential generator versus R's built-in `runif()`: trace plot, autocorrelation, and histogram for each.
* @fig-box-muller — Normal samples generated by the Box-Muller transform, compared with R's built-in `rnorm()`: histogram and QQ plot for each.
* @fig-lln-clt-gamma — Law of Large Numbers and Central Limit Theorem for the sample mean of Gamma(2,1) draws: raw draws, their histogram, running averages converging to $\mu=2$, and standardized running means stabilizing to $N(0,1)$.
* @fig-mc-pi-darts — 1,000 uniform points ('darts') thrown at the $[-1,1]^2$ square; the fraction landing inside the inscribed circle gives a Monte Carlo estimate of $\pi$.
* @fig-prop-mse-plot — Simulated MSE (with 95% Monte Carlo error bands) of $\hat p_1 = S/n$ versus the smoothed $\hat p_2 = (S+1)/(n+2)$, across $n = 2, 10, 50, 100$.
* @fig-t-test-df100 — Null distribution of t-test p-values at df = 100 (nearly normal), for $n = 2$ and $n = 20$: uniform, as expected.
* @fig-t-test-df3 — Null distribution of t-test p-values at df = 3 (heavy tails), for $n = 2$ and $n = 20$: the tails distort the p-value distribution away from uniform.
* @fig-t-test-df1 — Null distribution of t-test p-values at df = 1 (Cauchy): the test breaks down completely, with p-values clustering near 1.
* @fig-t-test-n30 — Null distribution of t-test p-values at $n = 30$, df = 10 and df = 5: the Central Limit Theorem restores uniformity even with heavy-tailed data.
* @fig-t-test-power-df5 — Power of the t-test at df = 5 against a true mean $\mu = 0.5$, for $n = 30$ and $n = 60$.
* @fig-t-test-power-df3 — Power of the t-test at df = 3 against a true mean $\mu = 0.5$, for $n = 30$ and $n = 60$.
* @fig-perm-cor-illustration — Permutation distribution of $|\hat\rho|$ for non-normal, dependent data, with the observed correlation marked in red: it sits far in the right tail.
* @fig-perm-cor-normal-h0 — Null distribution of the permutation-test p-value for correlation, normal data: perfectly uniform, as with a standard analytical test.
* @fig-perm-cor-nonnormal-h0 — Null distribution of p-values for independent, non-normal data: the permutation test (left) stays uniform while the Pearson test (right) struggles.
* @fig-test-lm-sel-h0 — Null distribution of the naive p-value after picking the best-correlated of 20 predictors: massively inflated near 0, showing the false-positive cascade from optimization bias.
* @fig-perm-lm-sel-size-power — Null distribution of the permutation-corrected p-value after variable selection: uniform again, restoring valid size.
* @fig-power-regression-h0 — Null distribution of p-values for the best power transformation of $X$: naive selection (left) inflates the false-positive rate, while the permutation fix (right) restores uniformity.
* @fig-power-regression-power — Power of the permutation test to detect $Y = X^{1.5} + \epsilon$ (left) and $Y = X^{0.5} + \epsilon$ (right) against the null of no relationship.

### Optimization for Maximum Likelihood Estimation

* @fig-bernoulli-toy-likelihood — Likelihood of $\theta$ for three Bernoulli observations $y = (1,1,0)$: the maximum sits at $\hat\theta = \bar y = 2/3$.
* @fig-normal-loglik-score-curvature — Log-likelihood, score, and curvature for a normal mean at $n = 20$ and $n = 50$: the larger sample gives a sharper peak, a steeper score, and larger curvature.
* @fig-cauchy-loglik-by-n — Cauchy log-likelihood for samples of increasing size ($n = 50, 100, 200$) from a true location $\theta_* = 20$: the peak sharpens around the truth as $n$ grows.
* @fig-cauchy-loglik-variability — 50 repeated Cauchy log-likelihood curves at $n = 20$ versus $n = 200$: the curves cluster more tightly, and their maxima concentrate, as $n$ grows.
* @fig-scheme-fixed-point — Fixed-point iteration as a cobweb diagram: iterates walk toward the intersection of $g$ with the diagonal.
* @fig-scheme-bisection — Bisection on the score function: each iteration halves the bracket that contains the root.
* @fig-scheme-newton — Newton-Raphson following the tangent to the score (left), and one Newton step compared with one Fisher-scoring step from the same point (right).
* @fig-cauchy-single-obs — Single-observation Cauchy negative log-likelihood and its derivative: the derivative flattens in the tails, the region that defeats Newton-Raphson.
* @fig-scheme-golden — Golden section search: the interior point that survives (blue) is already correctly positioned for the next iteration, so only one new point (red) is evaluated per step.
* @fig-golden-tests — Golden section search applied to a smooth genetic-linkage log-likelihood (left) and to a non-differentiable function $|x-10|$ (right), with the located minimizer marked in red.
* @fig-nzp-loglik-score — Log-likelihood and score for the zero-truncated Poisson model, from simulated data with $\bar x$ overshooting the true $\lambda = 1.5$.
* @fig-nzp-convergence-plot — Error decay (log scale) of simple iteration, Newton-Raphson, and the method of scoring for the zero-truncated Poisson MLE: Newton's error curve bends downward, reflecting quadratic convergence.
* @fig-nzp-quadratic-approx — Zero-truncated Poisson log-likelihood versus its quadratic approximation at $\hat\lambda$, with the resulting Wald 95% interval marked.
* @fig-nzp-mle-vs-naive — Sampling distributions of the naive estimator $\bar x$ versus the MLE for a zero-truncated Poisson mean, $\lambda_{true} = 1.5$: the naive estimator is badly biased upward, the MLE is centred on the truth.
* @fig-hessian-ellipse — Contours of a quadratic log-likelihood: gradient arrows (green) point uphill perpendicular to the contours but not toward the maximum unless the ellipses are circular; the dashed axes are the eigenvectors of $J(\hat\theta)$, each with half-length $1/\sqrt{\lambda_j}$.
* @fig-logistic-data — Simulated logistic data: true success probability and observed responses.
* @fig-gd-zigzag — Gradient descent with an exact line search zig-zags across an elongated valley: each step is orthogonal to the next.
* @fig-conjugate-gradient — Conjugate gradient (blue) reaches the minimum of the same elongated quadratic in far fewer iterations than gradient descent (red).
* @fig-sgd-vs-newton — SGD (fine, noisy trajectory) versus Newton-Raphson (large steps, one per full pass through the data) converging to the same logistic-regression MLE.

### EM Algorithms

* @fig-q-average — Ten complete-data log-likelihood curves, their average, and the exact $Q$ function.
* @fig-tangent-bound — Three EM iterations viewed as successive tangent minorants of the observed log-likelihood.
* @fig-mixture-components — The observed density is a sum of two weighted normal components.
* @fig-mixture-shapes — Separation and mixing proportion determine whether the mixture is visibly bimodal.
* @fig-estep — Left: the responsibility at each $y_i$ is the red share of the total height.
* @fig-mix-data — Simulated mixture data, coloured by the (normally unobserved) component label.
* @fig-truncation — A density split at a cut point, and the two renormalized conditional densities.
* @fig-poisson-estep — The conditional distribution of a censored count is the Poisson pmf restricted to $\{0,1\}$ and renormalized.
* @fig-clustering — Three-component multivariate normal mixture with unequal covariances.
* @fig-hmm — A two-state hidden Markov chain with normal emissions; background shading shows the hidden state.

### Introduction to Bayesian Inference

* @fig-prior-likelihood-posterior — Left: a flat-ish prior $\pi(\theta)$ (dashed) and a likelihood $L(\theta)$ (solid) that is much more concentrated — the data are far more informative than the prior here.
* @fig-predictive — Red: the sampling density $P(y_{n+1}\mid\theta_j)$ for ten posterior draws $\theta_j\sim N(3, 0.8^2)$.
* @fig-beta-priors — Six Beta priors spanning flat, U-shaped, and concentrated shapes.
* @fig-beta-posterior-narrowing — Prior Beta(2,2) (dashed) and posteriors after $n=10,50,200$ observations with $\bar y=0.7$ held fixed.
* @fig-pg-predictive-dispersion — Posterior predictive $P(y_{n+1}\mid\mathbf y)$ (Negative Binomial, red) against a plug-in Poisson at the posterior mean rate (gray).
* @fig-nn-predictive-dispersion — Posterior predictive $N(\mu_n, \sigma^2(1+1/\kappa_n))$ (red, solid) against a plug-in $N(\mu_n,\sigma^2)$ at the posterior mean (gray, dashed).

### Numerical Quadrature

* @fig-logistic-transform — Equally spaced points in $y$ (red ticks, right panel) map to unequally spaced points in $x$ (red ticks, middle panel).
* @fig-convergence — Absolute error versus number of panels, log-log scale.
* @fig-prior-sensitivity — The same likelihood (red) combined with three priors (blue). $P(y)$ is the area under $L(\theta)\pi(\theta)$ (shaded), computed here by `integrate` for a single parameter as a sanity check.
* @fig-grid — Left: the posterior $L(\mu,w)\pi(\mu,w)$ on its natural scale.
* @fig-curse — Left: a correlated 2-D posterior inside a 12x12 grid; only the highlighted points carry non-negligible mass.

### Laplace Approximation

* @fig-poisson-gamma-density — Exact Gamma posterior (red) and the Laplace normal approximation (green) for n=5 and n=100.

### Rejection Sampling

* @fig-envelope-scatter — Left: target $f(x)=e^{-x^2/2}$ (unnormalized standard normal) under its Laplace envelope $g(x) = e^{1/2-|x|}$, with the two areas shaded.
* @fig-gamma-tests — Q-Q plots of rejection-sampled draws against the true Gamma(alpha,1) quantiles, for three of the test cases: the envelope produces exact draws regardless of alpha, only the cost per draw changes.
* @fig-ars — Histograms of adaptive-rejection-sampled draws against the true truncated-normal density (red), in three increasingly extreme truncation windows: ars matches the target exactly regardless of where the window sits, only the cost per draw changes (@tbl-ars-timing).

### Importance Sampling

* @fig-missed-mode — Top: the bimodal target f (firebrick) against the proposal g (steelblue) on a log density scale, with a rug of S = 2000 draws.

### Markov Chain Monte Carlo

* @fig-two-walks — Long-run state frequencies for the cyclic walk (left, converges to uniform on all ten states) and the reflecting walk (right, concentrates almost entirely at state 9).
* @fig-gibbs-demo — Gibbs sampler on 50 simulated N(10, 2^2) observations: trace plots and posterior densities for mu and sigma, with a vague prior.
* @fig-tnorm-mh — Random-walk MH targeting N(0, 2^2) truncated to [4, 5], for three step sizes.
* @fig-stepsize — Step size too small, about right, and too large: trace (top) and autocorrelation (bottom) for a random walk targeting N(0, 1).
* @fig-mh-stepsize-search — Preliminary MH runs at four step-size scales, targeting mu (top: trace, bottom: ACF after discarding 500 iterations).
* @fig-hmc-vs-rw — Target: bivariate normal with correlation 0.98.
* @fig-stan-sv — Simulated stochastic-volatility data (left) and posteriors of the persistence phi and innovation scale tau under the non-centred parameterization (true values 0.3 and 1, red lines): both intervals are wide, reflecting genuine weak identification from a single 200-point series, but both cover the truth.

## List of Tables

### Introduction to R and Quarto

* @tbl-class-performance-report — Class performance report: first 10 students, with category scores and the final course score.

### Computer Arithmetic

* @tbl-fexp-naive — Built-in exp() versus the naive Taylor series fexp()
* @tbl-fexp-debug — Debug trace for fexp(-50) showing catastrophic cancellation
* @tbl-fexp-robust — Robust fexp2() for negative arguments
* @tbl-variance-scan — One-pass versus two-pass variance as the data are shifted by M

### Random Numbers and Monte Carlo Methods

* @tbl-mc-pi-by-n — Monte Carlo estimation of pi across different sample sizes.

### Introduction to Bayesian Inference

* @tbl-bb-summary — Complete inference output, Beta(1,1) prior with n = 10, y = 7.
* @tbl-pg-summary — Complete inference output, Gamma(2,1) prior, n = 8 Poisson counts.
* @tbl-nn-summary — Complete inference output, $N(0, \sigma^2/1)$ prior with known $\sigma=2$, n = 15.

### Numerical Quadrature

* @tbl-rules-accuracy — Error of each rule with only $n=10$ panels, relative to `pnorm`.
* @tbl-quad-vs-mc — Estimated log marginal likelihood: product midpoint rule versus naive Monte Carlo, for two simulated data sets.
* @tbl-quad-convergence — Estimated log marginal likelihood as the number of grid points per axis increases, for the $n=100$ normal-data example.
* @tbl-compare-priors — Log marginal likelihood for data centred at 0: rows are the prior mean $\mu_0$, columns the prior sd $\sigma_\mu$ (w-prior fixed at N(0,1)).
* @tbl-compare-models — Log marginal likelihood under four values of the t-model degrees of freedom nu, fit to data simulated from a Gaussian and from a heavy-tailed t(df=2).
* @tbl-mode-far-away — Log marginal likelihood for data centred at mu = -5 and mu = -20 (sigma = 2, n = 100), prior mu_0 = 0, sigma_mu = 10, w_0 = 0, sigma_w = 10: the product midpoint rule (n = 100 points per axis) against a naive Monte Carlo run of 100,000 draws from the prior.

### Laplace Approximation

* @tbl-poisson-gamma-error — Laplace log marginal likelihood versus the exact value, and the posterior mean versus the Laplace mode, as n grows.
* @tbl-poisson-gamma-ci — Laplace mode/SE-based 95% interval versus the exact Gamma posterior mean/sd-based interval, n = 20.
* @tbl-three-way — Log marginal likelihood by four methods, for data locations mu_hat = 0, -5, -20 (n_eff = 3, sigma = 1, prior N(0, 5^2) on mu).

### Rejection Sampling

* @tbl-rnorm-reject — Theoretical vs. simulated acceptance rate and sample moments for the Laplace-envelope normal sampler.
* @tbl-envelope-threshold — Minimum of log g(x) - log f(x) over x > 0, for several alpha.
* @tbl-gamma-tests — Acceptance rate falls sharply as alpha grows: the Cauchy envelope is tuned to match curvature at alpha = 2 and gets looser as the Gamma density becomes more Gaussian-shaped further from that point.
* @tbl-ars-timing — Adaptive rejection sampling (ars) vs naive rejection sampling from an untruncated N(0,1): naive sampling degrades catastrophically as the truncation window moves into the tail, while ars does not, because it never wastes draws outside [lb, ub] in the first place.

### Importance Sampling

* @tbl-is-t-examples — Four calls to `is_t_interval()` with S = 5000: a finite c2 is well-behaved at every df, c2 = Inf reproduces the divergent case, badly at df = 1 and only deceptively well at df = 30.
* @tbl-marlik-merged — Log marginal likelihood for a freshly simulated data set at each sample size n: truth by grid quadrature, against single runs of importance sampling (S = 2000) from a Laplace-shaped proposal and from the prior.

### Markov Chain Monte Carlo

* @tbl-gibbs-summary — Posterior summaries from the Gibbs sampler (after discarding a 200-iteration burn-in).
* @tbl-gibbs-censored — Recovering mu and sigma from data rounded down to the nearest 10, n = 200.
* @tbl-mh-vs-gibbs — Posterior mean and sd from Metropolis-Hastings versus Gibbs sampling, same data and priors: the two exact samplers of the same posterior agree up to Monte Carlo error.
* @tbl-stan-vs-hand — Posterior mean and sd: hand-written Gibbs and Metropolis-Hastings versus Stan's NUTS sampler, same data, priors, and model.
* @tbl-stan-sv — Posterior summaries for the stochastic-volatility model's top-level parameters, non-centred parameterization: Rhat near 1 and effective sample sizes in the hundreds indicate the chains have converged and mixed, in contrast to the centred version.
